AGREEMENT OF LEASE
Commercial premises · Oakridge Business Park
1. PARTIES
1.1 This agreement of lease is entered into between Oakridge Property Holdings (Pty) Ltd
(sample), registration number 2009/000000/07 (“the Landlord”), and Marula Office Supplies
(Pty) Ltd, registration number 2014/000000/07 (“the Tenant”).
1.2 The parties record that the Tenant has inspected the Premises and wishes to hire them on the
terms of this lease.
2. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION
2.1 In this lease, unless the context indicates otherwise, the following words have the meanings
given to them below:
2.1.1 “Building” means the office building known as Oakridge Business Park, erected on Erf 000,
Sampleton, together with its parking areas and grounds;
2.1.2 “Business Day” means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday in the Republic
of South Africa;
2.1.3 “Commencement Date” means 1 February 2024;
2.1.4 “Common Areas” means those parts of the Building intended for use by all tenants, including
entrances, passages, lifts, toilets and landscaped areas;
2.1.5 “Deposit” means the amount referred to in clause 6.1;
2.1.6 “Landlord's Agent” means any managing agent appointed by the Landlord from time to time
and notified to the Tenant in writing;
2.1.7 “Lease Period” means the period commencing on the Commencement Date and ending on 31
January 2027, both days inclusive, and “Expiry Date” means the last day of that period;

2.1.8 “Operating Costs” means the Tenant's proportionate share of the costs referred to in clause 7,
calculated on the basis of the rentable area of the Premises as a percentage of the rentable area
of the Building, being 8.6% (eight comma six percent);
2.1.9 “Premises” means Unit 4, Oakridge Business Park, 12 Sample Road, Sampleton, measuring ap-
proximately 412 m² (four hundred and twelve square metres), as shown on the plan in Schedule
1;
2.1.10 “Prime Rate” means the publicly quoted base rate of interest at which the Landlord's bankers
lend on overdraft, as certified by any manager of that bank;
2.1.11 “Rent” means the monthly rent for the relevant year of the Lease Period set out in Schedule 2,
excluding VAT;
2.1.12 “VAT” means value-added tax levied in terms of the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991.
2.2 Clause headings are for convenience only and shall not be used in interpreting this lease. Words
importing the singular include the plural and vice versa.
2.3 Where any number of days is prescribed, it shall exclude the first and include the last day, un-
less the last day falls on a day that is not a Business Day, in which case the last day shall be the
next Business Day.
3. LETTING AND HIRING
3.1 The Landlord lets to the Tenant, who hires, the Premises together with the right to use the
Common Areas in common with other tenants of the Building.
4. DURATION
4.1 This lease shall endure for the Lease Period, being a period of 3 (three) years.
4.2 The Tenant shall take occupation on the Commencement Date. The Landlord shall not be liable
for any delay in giving occupation caused by a previous occupant holding over.
5. RENT
5.1 The Tenant shall pay the Rent, together with VAT, monthly in advance on or before the first
Business Day of each month, without deduction or set-off, into the bank account nominated by
the Landlord in writing.
5.2 The Rent shall escalate on each anniversary of the Commencement Date by 8% (eight percent)
of the Rent payable in the immediately preceding year, as reflected in Schedule 2.
5.3 Any amount not paid on due date shall bear interest at the Prime Rate plus 2% (two percent),
calculated daily and compounded monthly, from due date until the date of payment.

6. DEPOSIT
6.1 Before taking occupation, the Tenant shall pay the Landlord a deposit equal to two months'
Rent at the rate applicable in the final year of the Lease Period, being R64 000.00 (sixty-four
thousand rand).
6.2 The Landlord shall hold the Deposit as security for the Tenant's obligations under this lease and
may apply it towards any amount owing by the Tenant. The Tenant may not set off the Deposit
against Rent.
6.3 The Deposit, less any amount owing, shall be refunded within 14 (fourteen) days after the
Tenant has vacated the Premises and the Landlord has inspected them.
7. OPERATING COSTS AND MUNICIPAL CHARGES
7.1 In addition to the Rent, the Tenant shall pay its Operating Costs in respect of any increase in
rates and taxes, refuse removal and insurance premiums levied on the Building above the
amounts levied in the first year of the Lease Period.
7.2 Electricity and water consumed in the Premises shall be measured by sub-meter and paid by
the Tenant monthly on presentation of the Landlord's statement, at the tariff charged by the
local authority.
7.3 The Tenant shall be liable for the cost of any separately metered air-conditioning serving only
the Premises.
8. USE
8.1 The Premises shall be used as offices and for the storage of office stationery incidental to the
Tenant's business, and for no other purpose.
8.2 The Tenant shall comply with the rules of the Building issued by the Landlord from time to time
and with all laws and by-laws relating to the use of the Premises.
9. MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS
9.1 The Tenant shall keep the interior of the Premises, including all glass, doors, locks, light fittings
and floor coverings, in good order and repair, fair wear and tear excepted.
9.2 The Landlord shall maintain the roof, exterior walls, structure and main services of the Building,
and the Common Areas.
9.3 The Tenant shall notify the Landlord in writing of any defect for which the Landlord is respons-
ible. The Tenant shall have no claim against the Landlord unless the Landlord fails to remedy
the defect within a reasonable time after notice.

10. ALTERATIONS
10.1 The Tenant shall make no structural alterations or additions to the Premises without the
Landlord's prior written consent. Any approved alterations shall, at the Landlord's election, be
removed or remain on termination, without compensation.
11. INSURANCE
11.1 The Landlord shall insure the Building against fire and other risks for its full replacement value.
The Tenant shall insure its own contents, stock and fittings.
11.2 The Tenant shall not do anything that may increase the premium on, or void, the Landlord's
insurance.
12. ACCESS AND INSPECTION
12.1 The Landlord and its agents may enter the Premises at reasonable times, on reasonable notice,
to inspect them, carry out repairs or show them to prospective tenants or purchasers.
13. SIGNAGE
13.1 The Tenant may, at its cost, display its name on the Building directory board and at the entrance
to the Premises in a form approved by the Landlord.
14. CESSION AND SUBLETTING
14.1 The Tenant shall not cede its rights, sublet the Premises or give up possession of any part of
them without the Landlord's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
15. BREACH
15.1 If the Tenant fails to pay any amount on due date, or breaches any other term of this lease and
fails to remedy that breach within 7 (seven) days of written notice, the Landlord may cancel this
lease, without prejudice to any claim for damages.
15.2 In any dispute arising from cancellation, the Tenant shall continue to pay an amount equal to
the Rent monthly in advance while it remains in occupation, without prejudice to its rights.
16. HOLDING OVER
16.1 If the Tenant remains in occupation after the Expiry Date without a new lease being concluded,
it shall do so on a monthly basis on the terms of this lease, terminable by either party on one
calendar month's notice.
17. LANDLORD'S HYPOTHEC
17.1 The Tenant records that it is aware of the Landlord's tacit hypothec over movable property on
the Premises to secure amounts owing under this lease.

18. RENEWAL
18.1 The Tenant shall have the option to renew this lease for a further period of 3 (three) years on
terms to be agreed.
18.2 The Tenant shall exercise the option by written notice to the Landlord given not less than two
calendar months before the Expiry Date.
18.3 If notice is not given as required, the option lapses.
18.4 If the parties cannot agree the Rent for the renewal period within 30 (thirty) days of the option
being exercised, it shall be determined by an independent valuer appointed by the chairperson
of the local property owners' association, acting as an expert and not an arbitrator.
19. PROTECTION OF PERSONAL INFORMATION
19.1 Each party shall process personal information received from the other only for the purposes of
this lease and in accordance with the Protection of Personal Information Act 4 of 2013.
20. DOMICILIUM AND NOTICES
20.1 The parties choose as their domicilia citandi et executandi the addresses set out in Schedule 1,
at which all notices and legal process may be delivered.
20.2 Any notice given in terms of this lease shall be in writing. A notice sent by email shall be
deemed received on the first Business Day after it is sent.
21. GENERAL
21.1 This lease constitutes the whole agreement between the parties. No variation or cancellation
shall be of any effect unless reduced to writing and signed by both parties.
21.2 No indulgence granted by a party shall constitute a waiver of any of that party's rights.
21.3 The parties consent to the jurisdiction of the Magistrate's Court having jurisdiction over the
Premises, notwithstanding that the amount in dispute may exceed that court's jurisdiction.
21.4 The Tenant shall pay the Landlord's legal costs, on the attorney-and-client scale, of enforcing
any of the Tenant's obligations.
21.5 This lease may be signed in counterparts, each of which is an original and which together con-
stitute one agreement.
